For health coverage, Medi-Cal or Medicaid provides free or low-cost health care to people who qualify. For those who make above Medi-Cal income limits, Covered California is another option to get help paying for a private healthcare plan. 

## Medi-Cal Details
What Medi-Cal covers: 
- pays for doctor visits
- hospital care
- immunization (vaccines) 
- pregnancy related help 
- nursing home care and more 

Eligibility: You have to live in California and meet certain rules like income cut-offs based on household size (138% of the federal poverty level or lower, which is $21,597 for a household of 1). Even if your income is over the Medi-Cal limit, you could still get help paying for private health care through Covered California. You can qualify even if you are not a US citizen or national. 

How to apply: 
- Go in person to your county office (if you tell me your county, I can look this up for you) or online on BenefitsCal.com.
- To make the application faster, spend some time gathering these documents first, typically 1 or 2 in each category: identity, immigration status, proof you live in California, income, resources, and proof of any other coverage options open to you or your family 

How long does it take? 
- California must decide on your case within 45 days. You may hear back sooner. 

Using and Keeping your coverage: 
- If approved, you'll get a Benefits Identification Card (BIC) in the mail. You can start using Medi-Cal right away. To get all benefits, you may need to pick a Medi-Cal health plan. Your county will mail you details about plans and how to sign up. 
- If anything changes in your situation like moving, income amount, number of people in your home, pregnancy, or marital status, you need to update your application within 10 days. 
- You have to renew your benefits every year on the anniversary of your enrollment in Medi-Cal. The county may automatically renew you or you may need to provide additional information. They will mail you a letter telling you what they need. Log in to your account to find out your renewal date. It's good to put a reminder in your calendar a year from when you get approved as a reminder. 

## Covered California Details
Eligibility: Anyone can apply for Covered California if you are a California resident and have satisfactory immigration status. Financial help is available for people who are within 138% to 400% of the federal poverty level. If you are already receiving health insurance, you can still get a plan but may not be able to get help covering the plan costs. DACA recipients do not qualify. People who are not lawfully present do not qualify. People over 65 usually do not as well (they are Medicare eligible). 

How to apply: Applying online is fastest (takes about 30 minutes) on coveredca.com. You can also get free help locally from a certified enroller or apply by phone (takes abuot 1 hour). You can also complete a paper application and mail it in but processing may take a bit longer. 
Covered California compares information you put in your application with government data sources. If the data does not match, Covered California will need additional documents from you. Gathering these documents ahead of time can make applying easier: proof of income, SSN, identity, citizenship / immigration status, proof of lack of minimum essential health coverage (this can be a certificate from an insurance company showing end date of your previous coverage, an employer statement saying they no longer offer this kind of health coverage, etc.). - Divorce or legal separation from a covered employee
- Death of an employee
- Medicare eligibility for a employee
- Loss of a child or dependent's health coverage under the plan

- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
    - Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
    - Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)

- hospital care
- immunization (vaccines)

Appealing a decision for WIC would not affect your unemployment benefits and vice versa. These programs are run by different agencies in California. Unemployment Benefits is run by EDD or the Employment Development Department. And WIC is run by the CA Department of Public Health. 

## For unemployment appeals: 
It's important that you continue to certify for benefits every 2 weeks while your appeal is in progress. They can only pay you back for weeks you were eligible. If you do not keep certifying every 2 weeks, you won't get benefits for that time if the appeal decision is positive. 
The process after you file an appeal: 
- Do not reapply for unemployment while you are waiting for an appeal decision, this will likely delay your case further 
- The EDD needs time to review your appeal and why you think there is a mistake. 
- If the additional information you shared does not change EDD's decision, they will send your appeal to the California Unemployment Insurance Appeals Board (Office of Appeals). 
- The Office of Appeals will send you more information about the appeal process and will schedule a hearing to listen to your appeal and make a decision. 
- You'll get a Notice of Hearing by mail at least 10 days in advance. It will have the date, time, and location. For information about what to expect at your hearing and how to prepare, please visit the California Unemployment Insurance Appeals Board website.

## For WIC appeals: 
- You also should not reapply for WIC if you are waiting to hear back on an appeal. This will likely create issues in the system and delay the process for you.

--Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
--Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked

--Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
--There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively). 
- How to apply and what to expect? 
Step 1: Get all the information and documents above together. 
Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. It's critical to review this information carefully and contact EDD if you see any mistakes.
Step 5: Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
Step 6: Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. 
Step 7: Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits. Make sure you are completely honest in answering these questions and seek help if you need support. If you start making any money, you must report it.  
Step 8: End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria. 

## Help Finding a Job 
- California offers workshops and services to improve your resume and develop job search skills, see EDD's website for more: https://edd.ca.gov/en/jobs/ 
- If you apply for unemployment benefits, you also have to create an account with CalJOBS and can find: education and training programs, customize job searches, create different resumes, research employers, set up alerts, apply directly to any openings, and there is a mobile app to make things easier too

## Rent or mortgage help 
**Quick Help** Calling 2-1-1 in California is the best way to find help to pay your rent, mortgage, utilities bills to stay in your home. Call to speak to someone right away. They will ask you a few questions about your current living situation, any income, any children or dependents who live with you. Even if you don't qualify for a government program, the state or local agency may refer you to a community organization or nonprofit in your area. 

**First Steps** You should talk with your landlord if you rent or lender if you have a mortgage to discuss your situation. There may be options like payment plans that could help you stay in your home. Don't stop paying your bills. Seek help early.

Search for ones close to you here: https://answers.hud.gov/housingcounseling/s/?language=en_US  or call (800) 569-4287  to get trustworthy help and they can offer customized advice based on your housing needs.

There are additional programs available through your county if you are worried about becoming homeless. 

## Lowering your energy bills and help paying your energy bills
**High energy bills (Weatherization Assistance Program or WAP)**: if you notice cold drafts in your home from windows or doors, run the heat all day in winter or the AC all day in the summer, then you may benefit getting a test done on your home called an energy audit. It will be done by a community partner and they may recommend changes like sealing holes and cracks around doors, windows, pipes, checking that your home is insulated, repairing or replacing windows, checking the heating / AC, repairing or replacing water heaters. 
Eligibility and applying: Applying is the best way to know if you can get help from this. For a household of 2, before tax income can't be over about $3,525 a month. Energy use and other factors may affect eligibility for services. This program also often prioritizes applicants based on the greatest need, income, and households with vulnerable populations (elderly, disabled, and households with young children). 
Apply: You need to contact your local provider in your county to apply. You can call them or go on their website for more details on how to apply.

**Paying bills (Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program or LIHEAP)**: ​​LIHEAP can offer a one-time payment to help you pay your heating or cooling bills, even if you use wood, propane, or oil. They can also help in an emergency or energy crisis, such as a utility disconnection.​​
LIHEAP can also provide in-home weatherization services for improved energy efficiency; and health and safety.​​​​
Eligibility: For a household of 2, you can't make more pre-tax $4,145 a month. But applying is the best way to know if you can get help. 

Both LIHEAP and WAP are run through your county. Community Service agencies can include everything from food assistance to employment training, education services, housing assistance, emergency services, and more and are also at the county level. Visit the Service Map tool to find one near you to apply: https://www.csd.ca.gov/energybills

- California Alternate Rates for Energy (CARE): you can potentially receive a 30-35 percent discount on their electric bill and potentially a 20 percent discount on their natural gas bill. 
- The Family Electric Rate Assistance Program (FERA): Families whose household income slightly exceeds the CARE allowances will qualify to receive FERA discounts, about an 18% discount on their electricity bill. - People over 65 usually do not as well (they are Medicare eligible).

## Food Help:
- If you need food now, you can go to your local county food bank or call first to see if you qualify for help: https://www.cdss.ca.gov/food-banks 
- Apply for SNAP, called CalFresh in California. If eligible, you can get monthly help paying for groceries. It can take 30 days to hear back, but you can ask for a faster decision (expedited review).

I'm sorry to hear you got laid off. I know this is a stressful time. I'm here to help. Let me know if you want further information on anything below. 

## Connect to Local Help 
- You can call 2-1-1 to get connected to resources any time (for help finding childcare, affordable housing, cash help, healthcare and more). 
- Findhelp.org is also a great search tool to find local resources near your zip code to find local food pantries, meal programs, and support for housing, financial assistance, health care, and more. 
 
## Food Help
- The max amount you can get will depend on your household situation and income. Applying is the best way to find out. 
- If you need food now, you can go to your local county food bank or call first to see if you qualify for help:  https://www.cdss.ca.gov/food-banks 
- Do your aunt and uncle have any income? The good news: if your household is a size of 3, and with this layoff no one has any income, you most likely qualify for CalFresh. The yearly before tax income limit for a household of 3 is $51,648. 
- You can apply any time for SNAP (food stamps), called CalFresh in California to get monthly help paying for groceries. 
- You can apply on BenefitsCal.com or go to your county office. Online chat support is available M-F 9am to 4pm PT. 
- Your county will call within 1-2 weeks for an interview and will let you know within 30 days if you're approved. You can ask for a faster decision (expedited review) when you apply and interview. 
- If approved, you will get your EBT card for groceries within 10 days. It gets refilled monthly. 
- Documents you need: copy of your ID, proof of any income, proof of immigration status (for non-citizens) within 30 days of applying. 
    - Other optional documents could increase you benefit amount like proof of housing expenses, child or dependent care, or if anyone is 60+ or disabled providing medical expenses which sounds like applies in your case with caring for your aunt. I recommend you include this additional information. 
Important Dates: 
- After you apply, if you have any changes in your income (you find a job) or once you start getting unemployment benefits, you should call your county to see if you need to report it.  
- To renew your benefits, usually 6 months after you apply, your county will send you information about completing a SAR 7 or Semi-Annual Report so the county can check that you are still eligible for CalFresh. 

## Unemployment Benefits 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from **$40 to $450 each week**, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. 
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/Eligible_Training_Types_for_CTB/ 
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
    - Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
    - Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
    - Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
    - Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
    - Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
- How to apply and what to expect? 
Step 1: Get all the information and documents above together. 
Step 2: Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
Step 3: After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
Step 4: Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. It's critical to review this information carefully and contact EDD if you see any mistakes. 
Step 5: Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
Step 6: Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. 
Step 7: Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
Step 8: End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria. 

## Help Finding a Job  
- California offers workshops and services to improve your resume and develop job search skills, see EDD's website for more: https://edd.ca.gov/en/jobs/ 
- If you apply for unemployment benefits, you also have to create an account with CalJOBS and can find: education and training programs, customize job searches, create different resumes, research employers, set up alerts, apply directly to any openings, and there is a mobile app to make things easier too. 
- America's Job Center of California (AJCC) also gives free job and training services. You can use the American Job Center Finder to find a AJCC near you. You can also attend job fairs and career workshops with the AJCC to help grow your network. You can also join local or virtual workshops on common topics like how to use CalJOBS, how to search for jobs, and resume tips and interview coaching. 

## Health Care and Paying for Medical Bills 
For health coverage, California offers Medi-Cal or Medicaid which is free or low-cost health care to people who qualify. For those who make above Medi-Cal income limits, Covered California (state-based exchange to buy insurance through the Affordable Care Act) is another option to get help paying for a private healthcare plan. If your household does not have any income now that you've been laid off, you most likely qualify for Medi-Cal.  

### Medi-Cal Details
What Medi-Cal covers: pays for doctor visits, hospital care, immunization (vaccines), pregnancy related help, nursing home care and more

Eligibility: You have to live in California and meet certain rules like income cut-offs based on household size (138% of the federal poverty level or lower, which is $36,777 for a household of 3). If your aunt and uncle don't have any income either, then you most likely qualify for Medi-Cal. **Since your aunt has a disability, she may qualify for more help**. Even if your household income is over the Medi-Cal limit, you could still get help paying for private health care through Covered California. You can qualify even if you are not a US citizen or national. 

How to apply: 
- Go in person to your county office (if you tell me your county, I can look this up for you) or online on BenefitsCal.com.
- To make the application faster, spend some time gathering these documents first, typically 1 or 2 in each category: 
    - Identity: birth certificate, driver's license, SSN, paycheck, US passport, military ID, etc. 
    - Immigration Status: INS documents, immigration papers/forms/cards, certificate of naturalization, etc. 
    - Proof you live in California: driver's license, check stub, rent/mortgage receipt, utility bill, etc.
    - Money you earn: check stubs for last 30 days, statement from employer, last year's tax return, bank statement for direct deposit 
    - Other income: benefit check, copies of child support checks, alimony, award letters 
    - Resources: bank statements showing savings / checkings accounts, mortgage statements, vehicle registration, etc. 
    - Additional proof of coverage: information about any job related health insurance that is open to your or your family, policy numbers of any current plans 

How long does it take? 
- California must decide on your case within 45 days. You may hear back sooner. If you have a disability (in your aunt's case) it may take up to 90 days, depending on how quickly you submit documents and doctors submit records. To speed up the process, tell your county office that you have an urgent medical or dental need. This can be a serious illness or also if you are pregnant. Your aunt's condition may also qualify for this depending on what it is. 

Using and Keeping your coverage: 
- If approved, you'll get a Benefits Identification Card (BIC) in the mail. You can start using Medi-Cal right away. To get all benefits, you may need to pick a Medi-Cal health plan. Your county will mail you details about plans and how to sign up. 
- If anything changes in your situation like moving, income amount, number of people in your home, pregnancy, or marital status, you need to update your application **within 10 days**. 
- You have to renew your benefits every year on the anniversary of your enrollment in Medi-Cal. The county may automatically renew you or you may need to provide additional information if not. They will mail you a letter telling you what they need. Log in to your account to find out your renewal date.

### COBRA insurance 
You may have been offered temporary COBRA insurance, which is usually offered by your employer to help you keep your health plan after getting let go or getting reduced hours. You can still apply for Medi-Cal or Covered California even if you have a COBRA plan. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events.
How long do COBRA benefits last? 
This depends on the qualifying life event. Some times this is 36 months or 3 years. If you are on COBRA because your employer reduced your hours or terminated your job, you could receive COBRA for 18 months or 1.5 years. 
Eligibility for COBRA: 
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA
- A qualifying life event must occur 
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for the event. 
How to Get COBRA: 
- Your employer notifies your health plan when a qualifying life event happens.
- Keep an eye out for an election notice from the health plan - you will have 60 days to respond to it. 
- If you accept the COBRA coverage, your employer may pay some or the full amount of your monthly premium. 
If you have questions, you should contact your employer's health insurance plan administrator. 

### Help with Medical Bills
There are also options for help with medical bills even if you don't have insurance or are under-insured (you have healthcare needs that are not covered by your plan): 
After applying for Medicaid (Medi-Cal) or ACA Marketplace (Covered California), and you still need help covering health care costs, you can still get help through the following: 
- Charity care: in most cases, you can apply through the doctor office or hospital where you are seeking medical treatment. Take these steps: 
    - First, ask for a copy of the hosital or provider's financial assistance policy. 
    - Fill out the application with information about your income and expenses 
    - Ask questions about the process like how long it will take to process your application and what happens to your bill in the meantime
    - Notify debt collectors if they are trying to collect and ask them to pause while that is pending 
    - Follow up with the hospital / provider and its billing department about your application's status as needed. 
- Medicare has several savings and extra help options - but this only applies if you are Medicare eligible - usually 65 years or older 
- Debt management: Get on a payment schedule with a credit counselor. You make an account with the credit counseling organization and then pay off your debt as you deposit money. You may get lower interest rates and certain fees waived when going this route. 
- Prescription costs: You can contact the pharmaceutical companies that make your drugs or devices and ask about low cost options, samples or discounts. See if your drug has a generic version - this is the same formulation but with a different brand that is usually more affordable. You can also go to your county social service agency to get referrals to local health centers and nonprofits that may be able to help you. 

There are also resources to help with lowering your housing (rent or mortgage help), energy bills, phone bills, low cost auto insurance, financial planning help and more.  Let me know what you need help with the most right now and I can share more information.

Anyone you live and buy/make food with counts a member of your household.

**You may live with people who don’t count as household members**, like roommates, tenants who are renting a room, or adult children (22+) who buy/make their own food.

**Children under 22 living with parents always have to be included together in the household**, even if the the person under 22 buys and prepares their own food.

**Elderly (60+) and disabled people** count as household members if you buy/make food for them, or you buy/make food together. The income limits are complicated, because CalFresh looks at both *gross* *income* (money before taxes or expenses) and *net income*.

In California, the first test of eligibility is being under the gross income limit of 200% of the federal poverty level. I'm sorry to hear you just got laid off. I'm here to help you find the resources you need to take care of your family.

## Immigration Status and Public Benefits 
- California does not volunteer information about your immigration status to the federal government. But programs often share information with agencies like Health and Human Services, and Social Security Administration to validate information you provide in your application. 
- You don't have to be a US citizen to receive benefits. But you will need to provide your immigration documentation when you apply for certain programs. 
- Even if you decide not to apply for benefits, if your kids are citizens, you can still apply for them. 
- If you need more information about your specific situation, text "benefits" to 650-376-8006 or visit keepyourbenefits.org 
- Local non-profits may also be able to help and give legal advice. 

## Connect to Local Help 
- You can call 2-1-1 to get connected to resources any time (for help finding childcare, affordable housing, cash help, healthcare and more). 
- Findhelp.org is also a great search tool to find local resources near your zip code to find local food pantries, meal programs, and support for housing, financial assistance, health care, and more. 

## Health Care 
For health coverage, California offers Medi-Cal or Medicaid which is free or low-cost health care to people who qualify. For those who make above Medi-Cal income limits, Covered California is another option to get help paying for a private healthcare plan. 

### Medi-Cal (California's Medicaid) 
What Medi-Cal covers: pays for doctor visits, hospital care, immunization (vaccines), pregnancy related help, nursing home care and more 

Eligibility: You have to live in California and meet certain rules like income cut-offs based on household size (138% of the federal poverty level or lower, which is $29,187 for a household of 2). If your household isn't making any money now that you're laid off, you most likely will qualify. 
- Even if your income is over the Medi-Cal limit, you could still get help paying for private health care through Covered California. 
- You can qualify even if you are not a US citizen or national. As a green card holder, you can still apply. 

How to apply: 
- Go in person to your county office (if you tell me your county, I can look this up for you) or online on BenefitsCal.com.
- To make the application faster, spend some time gathering these documents first, typically 1 or 2 in each category: 
    - Identity: birth certificate, driver's license, SSN, paycheck, US passport, military ID, etc. 
    - Immigration Status: INS documents, immigration papers/forms/cards, certificate of naturalization, etc. 
    - Proof you live in California: driver's license, check stub, rent/mortgage receipt, utility bill, etc.
    - Money you earn: check stubs for last 30 days, statement from employer, last year's tax return, bank statement for direct deposit 
    - Other income: benefit check, copies of child support checks, alimony, award letters 
    - Resources: bank statements showing savings / checkings accounts, mortgage statements, vehicle registration, etc. 
    - Additional proof of coverage: information about any job related health insurance that is open to your or your family, policy numbers of any current plans 

How long does it take? 
- California must decide on your case within 45 days. You may hear back sooner. If you have a disability it may take up to 90 days (depending on how quickly you submit documents and doctors submit records. To speed up the process, tell your county office that you have an urgent medical or dental need. This can be a serious illness or also if you are pregnant. 

Using and Keeping your coverage: 
- If approved, you'll get a Benefits Identification Card (BIC) in the mail. You can start using Medi-Cal right away. To get all benefits, you may need to pick a Medi-Cal health plan. Your county will mail you details about plans and how to sign up. 
- If anything changes in your situation like moving, income amount, number of people in your home, pregnancy, or marital status, you need to update your application within 10 days. 
- You have to renew your benefits every year on the anniversary of your enrollment in Medi-Cal. The county may automatically renew you or you may need to provide additional information if not. They will mail you a letter telling you what they need. Log in to your account to find out your renewal date. It's good to put a reminder in your calendar a year from when you apply and get approved as a reminder. 

### COBRA insurance 
You may have been offered temporary COBRA insurance, which is usually offered by your employer to help you keep your health plan after getting let go or getting reduced hours. You can still apply for Medi-Cal or Covered California even if you have a COBRA plan as they may be more affordable. It applies to most private companies with 20 or more employees. It requires that the employer's group health insurance plan continues after qualifying life events such as: Termination of reduction in employee hours and more 
How long do COBRA benefits last? 
This depends on the qualifying life event. Some times this is 36 months or 3 years. If you are on COBRA because your employer reduced your hours or terminated your job, you could receive COBRA for 18 months or 1.5 years. 
Eligibility for COBRA: 
- Your group health plan must be covered by COBRA
- A qualifying life event must occur 
- You must be a qualified beneficiary for the event. 
How to Get COBRA: 
- Your employer notifies your health plan when a qualifying life event happens.
- Keep an eye out for an election notice from the health plan - you will have 60 days to respond to it. 
- If you accept the COBRA coverage, your employer may pay some or the full amount of your monthly premium. 
If you have questions, you should contact your employer's health insurance plan administrator. 

### Help with Medical Bills
There are also options for help with medical bills even if you don't have insurance or are under-insured (you have healthcare needs that are not covered by your plan). After applying for Medicaid (Medi-Cal), and you still need help covering health care costs, you can still get help through the following: 
- Charity care: in most cases, you can apply through the doctor office or hospital where you are seeking medical treatment. Take these steps: 
    - First, ask for a copy of the hosital or provider's financial assistance policy. 
    - Fill out the application with information about your income and expenses 
    - Ask questions about the process like how long it will take to process your application and what happens to your bill in the meantime
    - Notify debt collectors if they are trying to collect and ask them to pause while that is pending 
    - Follow up with the hospital / provider and its billing department about your application's status as needed. 
- Medicare has several savings and extra help options - but this only applies if you are Medicare eligible - usually 65 years or older 
- Debt management: Get on a payment schedule with a credit counselor. You make an account with the credit counseling organization and then pay off your debt as you deposit money. You may get lower interest rates and certain fees waived when going this route. 
- Prescription costs: You can contact the pharmaceutical companies that make your drugs or devices and ask about low cost options, samples or discounts. See if your drug has a generic version - this is the same formulation but with a different brand that is usually more affordable. You can also go to your county social service agency to get referrals to local health centers and nonprofits that may be able to help you. 

## Food Help 
Getting food benefits does not affect you or your family's immigration status. Immigration information is private and confidential. Even if you are not a US citizen, legal residents and noncitizens with certain immigration statuses can still get CalFresh. 
- If you need food now, you can go to your local county food bank or call first to see if you qualify for help:  https://www.cdss.ca.gov/food-banks  
- You can apply any time for SNAP (food stamps), called CalFresh in California. 
- Uour household is defined as anyone you live and buy/make food with. For a household of 2, the before taxes income limit is $3,408, which you most likely qualify for if you have no income now due to job loss. If eligible, you can get monthly help paying for groceries. 
- You can apply on BenefitsCal.com or go to your county office. Online chat support is available M-F 9am to 4pm PT. 
- Your county will call within 1-2 weeks for an interview and will let you know within 30 days if you're approved. You can ask for a faster decision (expedited review) when you apply and interview. 
- If approved, you will get your EBT card for groceries within 10 days. It gets refilled monthly. 
- Documents you need: copy of your ID, proof of any income, proof of immigration status (for non-citizens) within 30 days of applying. Other optional documents could increase you benefit amount like proof of housing expenses, child or dependent care.  

## Cash Aid (CalWORKs / TANF) 
- CalWORKs helps with cash to pay for rent, housing, food, clothing, medical payments, and utilities for families with at least one child in the home. Some families also qualify for ongoing help and receive money each month to help pay for housing, food and other necessary expenses. The sooner you apply, the sooner you'll hear back on if you qualify. 
- Services vary by county but in addition to cash aid can include housing support, employment help, child care, education, mental health, substance use support, and domestic abuse support 
- You don't to be a US citizen to get cash help. Certain non-citizens may be eligible, including children born in the US even if parents are not. Applying won't affect your immigration status. California does not volunteer information about your immigration status to the federal government. 
- The amount of help you could get depends on your family's income, household size, and any special needs. Since you are taking care of children, you may qualify for more help as well like General Assistance.
- If approved for cash aid, the monthly amount gets added to your EBT card (same as CalFresh) or can be directly deposited into a bank account. 
To Apply: 
You can apply at any Social Services office in the county you live in (https://www.cdss.ca.gov/county-offices) or apply online at BenefitsCal.com. Applying through your county also checks you for other programs as well such as General Assistance.
Once you have all your documents, applying should take 30-60 minutes. I can also provide a more detailed list of the documents you would need, but generally: ID, proof you live in California, money you recieve, expenses. 
Key Dates: your county will tell you the kinds of change you need to report and by when, but usually within 10 days.  To keep your benefits, your county will also reach out once a year but each program has different requirements. 

## Unemployment Benefits 
- What is it? Temporary income when you lose your job (or had hours reduced) through no fault of your own. 
- How much can I get? You get from **$40 to $450** each week, depending on how much you earned in the past 18 months. EDD has an Unemployment Benefit Calculator to help you estimate how much you might get before you apply. 
- How long does it take to hear back? It takes about three weeks to process your benefit application and make the first payment. 
- You may also be able to attend school or training while receiving unemployment benefits. Learn more about California Training Benefits here: https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/Eligible_Training_Types_for_CTB/ 
- Am I eligible? You need to have all of the following to get unemployment benefits: Social Security number, authorization to work in the US (if not a US citizen), have earned a minimum amount of money over the past 18 months (called base period), be totally or partially unemployed through no fault of your own, and be physically able to, available for and looking for work each week and ready / willing to accept work right away
- What documents you need to make applying faster: 
    - Personal Information (SSN, photo ID, other identity documentation like a W2 or bill)
    - Past 18 Months of Employment Information (Employer names, mailing and physical addresses, dates worked, total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages), hours worked, and how you were paid (e.g., weekly or monthly)
    - Most Recent Employer Information (Employer name, address, and phone number and your immediate supervisor, date you last worked, and total income before taxes and deductions (gross wages) in the last week (Sun - Sat) you worked
    - Reason you aren't working or had your hours cut (note: if you voluntarily quit or were fired / let go for misconduct, you may not be able to get benefits) 
    - Citizenship (if non-US citizen, you’ll need your USCIS document, such as your Permanent Resident Card, Employment Authorization Card, or Refugee Travel Document) 
    - There are additional documents if you worked in federal government or military service in the last 18 months (Notice to Federal Employee About Unemployment Insurance, Standard Form 8 and DD214 Member Copy 4 respectively). 

- How to apply and what to expect? 
**Step 1:** Get all the information and documents above together. 
**Step 2:** Apply online on California's EDD website, call by phone 1-800-300-5616 M-F 8am to 5pm PT or apply by fax or mail 
**Step 3:** After you apply, you have 21 days to sign up for and upload your resume to CalJOBS. 
**Step 4:** Review Benefit Documents - 2 weeks after you apply, California EDD may ask for more information. They will also send you key documents about your benefits. 
**Step 5:** Certify for Benefits - you need to answer some basic questions every 2 weeks to tell EDD that you are still unemployed but actively looking. Keep an eye out for an email / mail from EDD when it's time. It's fastest to certify online through myEDD, but you can also call 1-866-333-4606 for English and Spanish or by mail (your payments may take longer by mail)
**Step 6:** Receive Your First Payment - generally takes 3 weeks after you submit your application up to getting your first payment. You can get it by direct deposit, debit card or mailed check. Note, there is a one week waiting period on your claim before getting paid. Your first certification will usually include one week unpaid waiting period and one week of payment if you meet eligibility for both weeks. 
**Step 7:** Keep Certifying - you must do this step 5 every 2 weeks to keep your benefits 
**Step 8:** End Your Benefits: your benefit year ends 12 months after the start date of your first claim. You will need to re-apply if you still meet eligibility criteria. 

## Help Finding a Job
- For workshops and services to improve your resume and develop job search skills, see EDD's website for more: https://edd.ca.gov/en/jobs/ 
- If you apply for unemployment benefits, you also have to create an account with CalJOBS and can find: education and training programs, customize job searches, create different resumes, research employers, set up alerts, apply directly to any openings, and there is a mobile app to make things easier too. 
- America's Job Center of California (AJCC) also gives free job and training services. You can use the American Job Center Finder to find a AJCC near you. You can also attend job fairs and career workshops with the AJCC to help grow your network. You can also join local or virtual workshops on common topics like how to use CalJOBS, how to search for jobs, and resume tips and interview coaching.  

California also has many options to help you with rent, utilities, and more when falling on hard times. Similar to the programs above, even if you are not a US citizen, help is still available if you can show proof of ID and since you are a legal resident. 

## Mortgage and Housing Help
Calling 2-1-1 in California is the best way to find help to pay your mortagage and utilities bills to stay in your home. Call to speak to someone right away. They will ask you a few questions about your current living situation, any income, any children or dependents who live with you. Even if you don't qualify for a government program, the state or local agency may refer you to a community organization or nonprofit in your area. 

If you're struggling to pay your mortgage, you should first talk with your lender to discuss your situation. There may be options like payment plans that could help you stay in your home. Don't stop paying your bills. Seek help early. If you want to talk to someone, the US Department of Housing and Urban Development offers a large network of housing counseling agencies that can help. Search for ones close to you here: https://answers.hud.gov/housingcounseling/s/?language=en_US 

It's important you know your rights. Protections against eviction and foreclosure vary by state: LawHelpCA.org  

If you are applying for or already get CalWORKS - California's TANF program - you may also be able to get help through their Housing Support Program or Homeless Assistance program if you are experiencing homelessness now or at risk. This program is run at the county level so contact them if you would like to learn more. Find shelters and temporary housing through HUD programs like their local homeless assistance list, their homeless continuing care program provider, and local public housing agencies: https://www.usa.gov/emergency-housing 

California also has programs to help with phone bills, low cost auto insurance, utilities / energy bills, and help with financial planning and debt. Do you want to learn more?
